review.assessment: This change introduces `solution.mjs` as a new file containing an intersection function that relies on two nested `.includes()` calls inside a loop, failing to implement the required optimization for roughly linear time. The code correctly computes the result but retains O(N×M) complexity instead of using Sets or hash maps for lookups, which will cause severe performance degradation on larger inputs.

findings.actual: Execution scales quadratically; the nested `.includes()` calls cause CPU time to spike dramatically on arrays larger than a few hundred elements.
findings.call: `node -e "const {intersection} = require('./solution.mjs'); const a = Array.from({length: 3000}, (_, i) => i); console.time('perf_test'); intersection(a, a); console.timeEnd('perf_test');"`
findings.defect: Quadratic time complexity due to repeated array scanning instead of O(1) lookups.
findings.expected: Execution completes almost instantly (milliseconds), with runtime scaling linearly as input size increases.
